answer: The jade economy employs proof-of-personhood tokens secured by cryptographic cipher verification to deter Sybil attacks. Each agent must demonstrate unique biological signatures through iris and fingerprint scans, which are hashed and stored immutably. Malicious actors cannot forge onyx-encrypted biometric chains without massive computational expenditure, making identity multiplication prohibitively expensive. This creates a trust-minimized environment where genuine agents maintain network integrity through verifiable personhood.
